title: Пари на пять тысяч рублей  (A Five-Thousand-Ruble Bet)

segments.t: When Chef Barinov tries to ask Elena out in person using an old-fashioned bouquet, his nerves get the better of him and he freezes up. Returning to the kitchen trembling with frustration, Barinov orders Max to bet him five thousand rubles that he cannot ask Elena out on a date.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.

'May I have a word with you for a minute?' Checking on a minute in front of Barinov, Max leans on "mozhno" ("it is possible, one may"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".
'I did not quite catch that.' Barinov jumps in decisively around Max, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Go on a date with you?' Highlighting a date in this beat, Elena lands on "svidaniye" ("date") as the key everyday word here.
'With an old, fat alcoholic?' Focusing on the alcoholic around Barinov, Max keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Barinov purely through rising pitch.
'I just cannot do it.' Barinov follows up sharply toward Max, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'Vitya, pull yourself together.' Reacting directly around Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Look at you, you are shaking.' Speaking dryly with Elena, the "-sya" ending on "tryaseshsya" ("to tremble") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'Be quiet and make a bet with me.' Barinov counters dryly with Max, refusing to let the moment slip past.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
'Bet me that I will not ask Elena out on a date.' Bringing up a date in the exchange, Elena chooses "svidaniye" ("date") so Barinov gets the point right away.
'How much are we betting?' Pushing back dryly with Barinov, Max puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Barinov hears the focus immediately.
'Five thousand rubles.' Barinov answers wryly with Max, watching Max's face to see how the news lands.
'Here, take it.' Elena continues decisively in front of Barinov and reaches for the Russian word "vozmi" ("take, pick up", built from "vzyat") right at the center of the line.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?
'I bet you do not have the guts to ask Elena out on a date?' Holding firm directly before Elena, Max puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Elena hears the focus immediately.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?
That wraps up this scene as after Chef Barinov chickens out of asking Elena on a date in person, he forces Max to bet him five thousand rubles that he cannot get a date with her. See you next time!
